discovery: Experimental demonstration of anyonic braiding statistics in the fractional quantum Hall effect

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological quantum matter
motivation: Since Leinaas and Myrheim showed in 1977 that two-dimensional quantum mechanics allows particles with statistics between bosons and fermions, anyons have been central to our understanding of topological order. For four decades they remained a theoretical prediction. In 2020 two complementary experiments settled the question. Nakamura and Manfra built Fabry-Pérot interferometers in ultra-clean GaAs heterostructures, grown with Manfra's molecular-beam epitaxy, and observed discrete phase slips that give the braiding phase of the ν=1/3 quasiparticles directly. Fève's group used an anyon collider and measured current cross-correlations that reveal fractional exchange statistics. Later work has extended these results to other filling fractions and to graphene. Together the experiments establish a new kind of quantum statistics in nature, show that topological order is a measurable physical property, and lay the experimental groundwork for topologically protected quantum computation.
